g.text: Loud on purpose. The alternative is a job that
appears to run every morning and delivers
One query, not a loop. Rank, this week's solves
and the revision queue all arrive with the row —
four round trips per person against a cold Neon
instance is the difference between a run that
finishes and one still going at breakfast.
Ordered most-recently-active first: that is what
The reason there is a second send rather than a
repeat. "You have already done your practice" at
6pm is noise, and two near-identical emails a day
is how people learn to ignore both.
drop anyone who has already practised today
Announced, never silent. A job that quietly mails
half its users looks identical to one that mailed
The budget is for the whole DAY across both runs,
and is shared with sign-in codes — overspending it
truncate, and log exactly how many were skipped
(streak alive / at risk / lapsed / dormant / new)
Rate limit, cold start, markdown, a preamble,
no API key — all the same here. Nothing about a
language model may stop the mail.
The model is forbidden from quoting statistics:
congratulating somebody on a streak they do not
have costs more trust than a plain template.
Greeting and subject follow the run, not the clock.
These messages cannot be un-sent, so forgetting
them because the run failed later would let the
next run spend the same budget again.
